claims.statement: src/app/globals.css defines a near-monochrome design-token palette (--background, --foreground, --surface, --border, --border-strong, --muted, --faint, --accent, --accent-foreground) with light and prefers-color-scheme:dark variants, reserving color for semantic meaning only via --overload-up, --overload-down, --calibrate, and --record tokens.
Tailwind's @theme inline block in globals.css re-exports the raw CSS variables as --color-* tokens consumed by utility classes, aliasing --color-danger to --overload-down.

The type scale is fixed to four steps (--text-display, --text-heading, --text-body, --text-caption) plus one named exception, --text-recap, which is reserved for the finish-recap hero only and is not a fifth general scale step.

The app uses exactly two border radii across the whole UI: --radius-card and --radius-control, applied via Card and control classes respectively, and a single capped content column via --container-page (max-w-page).

All motion tokens (animate-tick, animate-row-in, animate-rise, the sheet transition, the skeleton pulse) animate only transform/opacity in the 150-320ms range using one easing curve (--ease-snap), and a global prefers-reduced-motion:reduce rule collapses all animation/transition durations app-wide.

Sheet is the app's single overlay primitive: it drives a native <dialog> with showModal() for a built-in focus trap, and unifies Escape (dialog cancel event), scrim-tap, and a swipe-down-past-90px drag gesture into one dismiss() function that sets data-closing, waits EXIT_MS (250ms) to match the CSS transition duration, then calls dialog.close() and the caller's onClose.

Sheet exposes its dismiss handler to descendants via useSheetDismiss()/DismissContext so inner controls (e.g. a Done or Cancel button) trigger the identical animated close as Escape or scrim-tap; callers must render Sheet conditionally and unmount only after onClose fires, since unmounting immediately would skip the exit animation.

InfoButton is the app's single ⓘ pattern for helper prose: a 44px circle-i control that opens a read-only Sheet rendering the title as an h2, short body text, and a ghost Done button; info Sheets never carry destructive or save actions, which stay on the originating control's own dedicated confirmation Sheet.

Button/IconButton styling is split into plain (non-"use client") modules (button-styles.ts, icon-button-styles.ts) that export pure class-builder functions, separate from the "use client" components (button.tsx, icon-button.tsx), specifically so Server Components can style <Link> elements as buttons without becoming Client Components; calling a helper exported from a "use client" module from a Server Component can fail at runtime even though the build succeeds.

Button derives its pending/busy state either from an explicit pending prop or from useFormStatus() when the button is a submit inside a <form action>, so server-action submissions show a spinner without requiring local state management at each call site; IconButton mirrors this same pending logic and requires an aria-label prop.

Stepper implements press-and-hold auto-repeat and value-tick animation by reading the latest value through a ref (valueRef) inside events/effects rather than in render, avoiding stale closures during a hold, and uses a local text draft state to allow transient mid-edit values (e.g. "52." or "-") that only commit to a clamped numeric value on blur.

Card exposes exactly one shared surface (one radius, one border, one padding) with hierarchy expressed only through a tone prop (default/active/done) using border and opacity, never a second radius or shadow; callers derive tone from saved-set counts and the currently effective phase prescription rather than storing tone as separate data.

withViewTransition wraps a state update in document.startViewTransition and flushSync so elements with a matching viewTransitionName animate positionally; program-builder uses it for day and slot button-reorder (names vt-${day.id} and vt-${slot.id}), not phase reorder, and falls back to a synchronous plain update when startViewTransition is unsupported or prefers-reduced-motion:reduce is set.

Calendar is a shared, generic month-grid client component providing keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown) and grid/gridcell ARIA semantics with a markers map for day dots; it deliberately does not own mutation, replacement-conflict, or error handling, which are left to specific callers such as the weight calendar.

src/app/(app)/layout.tsx is a Server Component that performs the app's auth gate (Supabase getClaims(), redirecting to /login if unauthenticated) and wraps the client-side AppShell. AppShell reads usePathname and, inside Suspense, useSearchParams to decide chrome, embodying the server/client boundary: data loading and auth stay server-side while pathname-aware chrome, charts, clipboard, and search are client components.

AppShell renders a four-destination bottom TabBar (Lift, Track, Program, You) using per-tab match(pathname) predicates and aria-current; isTrackPath in src/lib/app-chrome.ts makes Track match /analytics, /analytics/*, and /history/... so Exercise review pages read as part of Track despite their /history URL segment.

hideAppChrome(pathname, search) hides the bottom tab bar on /session/[id] (including its /session/[id]/recap finish recap), /workout/next, /program/new, and /program/[id] when the mode=edit search param is set, because each of these routes owns Home (and, for recap, View recap/View workout) as its own sticky exit instead of the tab bar.

AppShell evaluates hideAppChrome with only the pathname (inside a Suspense fallback) before useSearchParams() resolves, and only re-evaluates with the search string once search params are available; this means /session/*, /workout/next, and /program/new are hidden immediately on navigation and never flash the tab bar, while the mode=edit branch (the only one needing search) can only apply once search params resolve.

Pins are a per-user display preference layered on IconButton and Sheet rather than a core data concept. PinButton and PinEditorButton call toggleExercisePin and update aria-pressed only after a successful result, showing the action error without flipping state on refusal. The editor Sheet lists Compounds and More lifts with search and a default-size ExerciseVisual per row. Unpinning a default compound hides its tile; pinning an extra adds one. A cap of 8 visible tiles (PIN_CAP) is enforced server-side by canPinExercise inside the toggle action, not by disabling the control in the editor.

The active workout's rest timer state lives in the session/[id] layout (not a leaf page) and is driven by an absolute end timestamp mirrored into sessionStorage, so a logged-set data refresh (e.g. PR/e1RM chip updates) cannot clear it and a hard remount can resume the same countdown; the session route's loading.tsx and error.tsx both render the same rest bar so navigation or error states never visually drop the timer.

Copy-density rules require: fixing unclear labels before adding captions, deleting developer/implementation notes (Web Audio, Notification API, Coach internals) outright rather than relocating them, moving how-it-works/legend/rationale prose behind the single InfoButton-to-Sheet pattern, keeping privacy/consent copy in dedicated confirmation Sheets rather than the Settings card surface or an InfoButton, and capping any other visible helper text at roughly six words or removing it.

The rest-complete-tone Settings checkbox is the canonical worked example of the copy-density rules: its caption explaining Web Audio, notification permission, and vibration behavior was deleted from the visible UI, and only the short why (two beeps in this tab; vibration is separate) survives, moved into an InfoButton Sheet next to the checkbox label.

The finish-recap screen reuses the animate-rise motion token for its hero number and record rows with staggered ~70ms delays, and record-gold styling (--record) is applied only to rows corresponding to an actual entry in workoutRecords, never to a no-record finish.

ExerciseVisual is the only exercise illustration: a decorative 16:9 rounded-control frame (alt empty, aria-hidden) with object-cover and a 1.35 center zoom. sm is 36x64 on rows and tiles; lg is 64x114 on the session slot header, planner cards, Exercise review header, and in-session history. Art is looked up by baseExerciseId, then exact exerciseId, then the non-custom id prefix before __, never by display name; unmapped, custom, or empty ids render IconDumbbell in the same box instead of a broken image.

AgentEntry is shell chrome, not a tab: when hideAppChrome is false and the path is not /coach or /coach/*, AppShell mounts a fixed Coach IconButton above the tab bar that opens an AgentChat Sheet. Immersive routes hide it by the same hideAppChrome gate as the tab bar.
